script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Romance
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Our HERO, JAMES (30s), a brilliant but introverted scientist, sits at a table, working on a laptop. He's lost in thought, his brow furrowed.

WAITRESS (20s) enters, setting down a steaming cup of coffee in front of him.

WAITRESS
(smiling)
You look focused, sir. Another cup on the house today?

JAMES
(nodding)
Yes, thank you.

WAITRESS
(leaning over the table)
You know, I've seen you here almost every day for weeks. You're always working on something new. What's your project this time?

JAMES
(looking up, slightly surprised)
I'm developing a new clean energy technology. It could change the world.

WAITRESS
(impressed)
Wow, that's amazing! I'm an artist, but I've always admired people like you who are driven by their passions and ambitions.

JAMES
(smiling)
Thank you. It's not always easy, but it's worth it.

INT. LABORATORY - NIGHT

James is in his lab, surrounded by beakers, test tubes, and machines. He's exhausted but determined, working late into the night.

Suddenly, his PHONE RINGS. It's a call from his LAB TECH, MARK (40s).

MARK (V.O.)
James, I've got some bad news. One of the test subjects for the new energy source has exploded.

JAMES
(pausing, concerned)
What? Were you hurt? Is anyone else injured?

MARK
(sighs)
No, I'm fine. But we need to shut down the lab and figure out what went wrong.

JAMES
(resigned)
Understood. I'll be there as soon as I can.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

The next day, James is back at the coffee shop, nursing a cup of coffee. The Waitress approaches.

WAITRESS
You look upset, James. Is everything alright?

JAMES
(shaking his head)
Something went wrong in the lab last night. One of the test subjects for my new energy technology exploded.

WAITRESS
(looking worried)
Oh no, are you okay?

JAMES
(nods)
I'm fine. But it sets me back significantly. I need to figure out what went wrong and find a solution.

WAITRESS
(placing a hand on his shoulder)
You'll get through this. You're brilliant, and you've come so far. Don't give up on your dreams.

JAMES
(looking up, determined)
Thank you. I won't give up.

INT. LABORATORY - DAY

James and Mark are in the lab, working together to figure out what went wrong. They're focused, determined to solve the problem and get back on track.

WAITRESS (V.O., off-screen)
(singing softly)
Don't give up, don't ever give up.

James and Mark look up, surprised to hear the Waitress's voice. She's standing in the doorway, holding a bouquet of flowers.

WAITRESS
I wanted to bring you some encouragement. I believe in you and your work. Keep going, James.

JAMES
(smiling)
Thank you. I will.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

James is back at the coffee shop, working late into the night. The Waitress comes over and sits down across from him.

WAITRESS
You've been here every night this week. Why not take a break? Go home, get some rest.

JAMES
(looking up, hesitant)
I can't. I need to figure this out.

WAITRESS
(placing a hand on his forearm)
James, I understand your ambition and your drive. But you're only one person. You can't do it all alone.

JAMES
(looking into her eyes)
Maybe you're right. Maybe I need help.

Waitress smiles, a genuine, warm smile.

WAITRESS
I'll be here for you, James. Whenever you're ready.

James smiles back, a newfound hope in his eyes.

JAMES
Thank you. I'll take you up on that.

FADE OUT.
